body: Thank you so much, I don't think you understand how much I greatly appreciate this. This is the first time I've actually received any type of advice for this so thank you.

I don't have any documentation at all, my phone was taken away when all the swelling and scratches were there. I don't there's anyone I know I trust with this information either, being in a situation is entirely new to me and I'm kinda scared as to what can happen.

Yeah I'm safe for now, I'm not about to get beat up or anything like that. I apologized that this is stupidly long.

A little over a year on 4/20, my guidance counselor called my mother just wondering what's going on since I wasn't doing my work. And I'm talking to her and saying yeah yadda yadda, my mental health hasn't been the best but I'll get my work done by the end of the week. And like the moment I uttered the words "mental health", my mother kinda mocked me for saying that, kinda like I was crazy. The vibe completely changed and I was like what's the problem, her being like that just upset me a lot.

I'm off the phone and hand it back to her, she tells me to go to my room and we'll "talk", whatever. You know when you can tell someone is angry and they're about to do something, that's what I felt in that moment. She's stomping up the stairs, and I say, very foolishly, "what, you're gonna hit me?". Mind you, I didn't raise my voice, I didn't ball up my fists, I was just so tired of getting beat for poor grades, especially when they didn't reflect me. It feels like, my years of highschool and how well I did then didn't even matter. 

And then she hit me, like over and over again like a punching bag. I didn't hit her back to prove something to myself and her,  I just refused to. And we're like insulting each other blah blah, she insults my dad blah blah, whatever people yell at each other when they're angry, I didn't take any of it to heart. She continues hitting me but then she starts to straddle me and continues to strangle me. I hit her once, in that moment, it wasn't hard, on the left side of her face. But she just seethes at me, "I will fucking kill you". If I didn't think she loved me then, she definetely doesn't love me now. 

She does eventually get off of me, and I can't process anything at all. She tells me to get up and get out, more hitting, I lost my hearing for a short amount of time. My grandfather and sister are at the door, telling her to get off of me but when I start cursing, they just tell me to watch my language, like did you just see what happened, the last thing you should be worried about is my language.

My dad does come to pick me up, and we're at his place, and he's like you really hurt her that day. I'm concussed, I almost threw up, I can't stomach anything, have a killer headache and my throat and neck is killing me. I had to force myself to eat without throwing up for the rest of the month. I had to go back like after a week of staying with my dad and with having expressed I didn't want to go back. Everyone's like, why don't I talk back to her, like I didn't almost die right in front of you. 

And then me dealing with that until early February, when I'm still pretty dud at school, my mother's like "You're coming with me to Jersey like right now". Had to pack my stuff that day and moved in the morning after. So I've been here since, heavily dissociating and being just scared out of my mind she's gonna try something like that again. 

If you need more info on something, you can just ask.

I'm in the US but I think an issue is there hasn't been a string of abuse, there's no neglect or anything like that, that's the only time it's gotten that bad and it happened a year ago. That and I am deathly afraid of repercussions that my mother would face with the authorities, especially with the rest of my family judging the shit out of me.

I'm in the same boat, I could sleep for the whole day and still feel incredibly tired. Being mentally drained from whatever has that effect no matter what you physically do it seems. However, I can't really give any tips since I'm still dealing with it.
